method: Real web research (WebSearch/WebFetch) against NFA Uganda, WDPA/Protected Planet, FAO, Ministry of Water & Environment publications, FSC Africa, CAO Ombudsman case records, and news/NGO reporting on Uganda forestry, conducted 2026-09-13. Covers the 15 highest-VOI catchment CFRs only (not all 276) -- prioritized by model contribution per the sprint's explicit instruction. Never infers availability from absence of restriction language; UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT used where sources genuinely disagree.

cfrs.rationale: NFA's own 2024 Forest Management Plan status table lists Mabira as having a currently VALID plan (2016-2026) -- the only one of these 15 CFRs confirmed valid. Zoned into strict nature reserve / buffer / production zones; an ecotourism concession operates under NFA in the western zone (licensee not named). Predominantly natural/mixed moist forest, not eucalyptus plantation -- legally zoned access, not open commercial availability.

sources.note: NFA 2024 FMP status table: Mabira listed valid 2016-2026

cfrs.rationale: 50-year NFA tree-farming license (pine + eucalyptus plantation, 80% planted). License held by Global Woods AG until end-2020, then taken over by Nile Fibre Board (NFB), a subsidiary of Nile Plywoods -- a DIRECT COMPETITOR to Evergreen. FSC Forest Management + Chain of Custody certified. NFB operates its own processing plant (Nakasongola) already consuming this output.

sources.note: 2021-04-01, license transfer to Nile Fibre Board, FSC certification

cfrs.rationale: Area figures conflict across sources (10,298 acres / ~4,167 ha per Wikipedia vs ~2,000 ha per a Monitor report). Presidential directive to degazette the reserve to formalize long-settled occupants. >80% of Nakasongola-area forest cover reportedly lost in the last ~20 years. Very low confidence this CFR contributes real standing roundwood.

16,382 ha, gazetted 1948. Nileply Ltd (Jinja plywood producer -- a DIRECT COMPETITOR to Evergreen) has planted ~1,500 ha of eucalyptus here under a confirmed commercial planting-rights arrangement. Remainder reportedly subject to a degazetting process for resettlement of previously-evicted villages. Mixed status: part committed to a competitor, part contested.

Area independently confirmed via WDPA (158.71 km2 / ~15,871 ha, site ID 40124). No species, management-authority, license, or activity evidence found despite dedicated search. A 2017 NFA lease tender for reserves in Kakumiro/Kibaale/Kagadi districts is geographically plausible but not confirmed to cover this specific reserve.

8,281 ha. 50-year license granted April 2005 to New Forests Company (NFC) -- pine + eucalyptus plantation, part of NFC's combined ~12 million trees planted across 3 sites. NFC is itself the commercial offtake destination (vertically integrated), not available third-party feedstock. Also carries an active CAO (IFC Compliance Advisor Ombudsman) complaint over evictions (filed Dec 2011 by Oxfam/Uganda Land Alliance).

9,383 ha. Same New Forests Company license program as Namwasa (2005, 50-year, pine + eucalyptus). Vertically integrated to NFC, not available to Evergreen. Same CAO Ombudsman case family (eviction disputes), with a later negotiated agreement recognizing NFC's legal operating rights.

9,165 ha licensed area (~4,300 ha actually planted), 50-year renewable license from 1996 to Busoga Forestry Company (BFC), a subsidiary of Green Resources AS (Norway). Hybrid eucalyptus clones + pine. BFC/Green Resources operates its own integrated products (utility poles, timber, charcoal/briquettes) -- vertically integrated, not available feedstock. Part of the estate is simultaneously being degazetted for resettlement (contested).

88.02 km2 (~8,802 ha), gazetted 1968, NFA direct management. Natural/mixed forest (106 tree species cited), with NFA's own description noting weak enforcement capacity. No license, concession, or processor relationship found -- confirmed natural estate under nominal NFA control but no evidence either way on commercial access.

sources.note: area, gazettement, biodiversity, NFA management, weak enforcement note

cfrs.rationale: Area figures conflict by ~2.5x across sources (6,079 ha vs ~15,021 ha). ~70% reportedly cleared by encroachers. An active, disputed NFA boundary re-demarcation and a separately reported contested 2022 land (re)allocation ('Mujuzi forest give-away') make this CFR's real status genuinely unresolved between conflicting accounts.

Academic (UFRIC) literature describes it as 'severely degraded' with restoration/replanting activity noted qualitatively, split into research sites 'Lwamunda A/B'. No area, license, species mix, or dated harvesting evidence found.

Only located reference: an academic Acacia senegal distribution paper naming it as an in-situ conservation site -- implies natural savanna/acacia woodland, not plantation, but no management, license, or area data found.
Only a bare geographic-location hint (Masaka District) found; nothing on area, management, species, or status located despite search.

Area and 1932 gazettement date independently confirmed via WDPA (~51.5-51.85 km2, site ID 40131), NFA-managed per WDPA governance type. A possible NFA budget-document reference to 'inventory of maturing crops in plantations' could not be verified to specifically cover this reserve -- flagged as an unconfirmed lead, not asserted.
